problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable optimization on R^d, permitting nonconvex objectives. There is a global lower bound ℓ with f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ; no minimizer attainment or convexity is required.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each oracle call returns (F(x,ω),F(y,ω)) using the same fresh sample ω for both queried points. Samples are IID across calls. Sample gradients G are unobserved. No moment bound or unbiasedness assumption is imposed on function values themselves. One budget unit counts a pair of evaluations.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, E[G(x,ω)]=∇f(x) and E‖G(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖₂^p≤σ^p, with 1<p≤2 and σ≥0. For p<2, finite variance is not required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is R^d with its Euclidean inner product and norm, for a positive integer d.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Every sample function is differentiable with gradient G and uniformly L-smooth: ‖G(x,ω)−G(y,ω)‖₂≤L‖x−y‖₂ for all ω,x,y, with L>0. Samples are IID. All parameters d, Ω, L, Δ, σ, p, ε and x0 are public; f, F, G and the sampling laws are hidden. Δ≥0 and ε>0.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return a measurable point X∈R^d with integrable gradient norm and E‖∇f(X)‖₂≤ε. The criterion uses the norm, not its square; no particular iterate selection is prescribed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The expectation includes algorithm randomness and the IID oracle sequence. Oracle expenditure is bounded by the supplied fixed budget, rather than only in expectation.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: An established stochastic zeroth-order formulation: smooth nonconvex optimization with shared-sample two-point evaluations, bounded heavy-tailed gradient moments, and expected first-order stationarity.

descriptionHtml:
Heavy-Tailed Two-Point Zeroth-Order Optimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥1, with a lower bound ℓ∈R and given starting point x0 satisfying f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ, where Δ≥0. The oracle returns two scalar values F(x,ξ) and F(y,ξ) using a shared sample ξ∼ν, with independent samples across calls. Each sample function F(⋅,ξ) has an L-Lipschitz gradient, where L>0; these gradients are unbiased for ∇f and have centered pth moments bounded by σp, where 1<p≤2 and σ≥0. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, with expectation over sampling and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x), where ∥⋅∥ denotes the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives d, the measurable sample space Ω, L, Δ, σ, p, ε, and x0∈Rd.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Objective and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere. There exists ℓ∈R such that f(x)≥ℓfor every x∈Rd,f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Sample smoothness). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and jointly measurable maps F:Rd×Ω→R,G:Rd×Ω→Rd. For every ω∈Ω, the function F(⋅,ω) is differentiable everywhere, and for every x,y∈Rd, ∇xF(x,ω)=G(x,ω),∥G(x,ω)−G(y,ω)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Unbiased gradients and heavy-tailed noise). For every x∈Rd, the map G(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under ν, and ∥G(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥p is integrable under ν. They satisfy Eξ∼ν[G(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥G(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥p]≤σp.

At call k≥0, the algorithm queries any pair (xk,yk)∈Rd×Rd and receives (F(xk,ξk),F(yk,ξk)). The sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν. They are independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Thus both values in a reply use the same sample, while distinct calls use independent samples. One oracle call returns this pair of scalar values; the budget counts such paired calls.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯∈Rd must be measurable, its gradient norm must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the samples and the independent algorithm randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f:Rd→R, d≥1, has a lower bound f∗ with f(x0)−f∗≤Δ. Samples F(⋅;ξ) have L-Lipschitz gradients G, with F,G jointly measurable, ∫G(x;ξ)dν=∇f(x) and ∫∥G(x;ξ)−∇f(x)∥pdν≤σp, with the corresponding integrability, 1<p≤2. Each oracle call returns two values sharing one sample; successive samples are IID with law ν. Target: ∫∥∇f(xout)∥dP≤ε. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedTwoPointZerothOrder

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Point (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : Point d

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := Point q.d → ℝ
  Query q := Point q.d × Point q.d
  Reply _ := ℝ × ℝ
  Output q := Point q.d
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.d ∧ 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 1 < q.p ∧ q.p ≤ 2 ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (F : Point q.d → q.Ω → ℝ) (G : Point q.d → q.Ω → Point q.d)
      (ν : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (ν : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, y) ω => (F y.1 ω, F y.2 ω) } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ f x) ∧ f q.x0 - lower ≤ q.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry F) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry G) ∧
    (∀ ω x, HasGradientAt (fun y => F y ω) (G x ω) x) ∧
    (∀ ω x y, ‖G x ω - G y ω‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (G x) (ν : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, G x ω ∂(ν : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖G x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ q.p) (ν : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖G x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ q.p ∂(ν : Measure _) ≤ q.σ ^ q.p)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedTwoPointZerothOrder
